immutability.unsupported: This storage backend has no Object Lock, so immutability cannot be configured for it. Object storage (S3) repositories can lock every backup they receive.
immutability.validateHint: Writes a locked test object, reads its retention back and tries to delete it — the only way to know the bucket really enforces what is configured here.
immutability.validateDirtyHint: Validates the SAVED setting, not the change above. Save first to check the new one.

change.enabled_zero: Backups written from now on will be locked. Nothing is stored here yet, so nothing is left behind.
change.enabled_one: Backups written from now on will be locked. The {{count}} restore point already stored was written without a lock and stays deletable until you apply immutability to it below.
change.enabled_other: Backups written from now on will be locked. The {{count}} restore points already stored were written without a lock and stay deletable until you apply immutability to them below.
change.strengthened_zero: The stronger setting — a longer period, a stricter mode, or both — applies to backups written from now on.
change.strengthened_one: The stronger setting — a longer period, a stricter mode, or both — applies to backups written from now on. The {{count}} restore point already stored keeps the lock it was written with: a written lock is never extended or strengthened by a settings change. Apply immutability to it below to bring it under the new one.
change.strengthened_other: The stronger setting — a longer period, a stricter mode, or both — applies to backups written from now on. The {{count}} restore points already stored keep the locks they were written with: a written lock is never extended or strengthened by a settings change. Apply immutability to them below to bring them under the new one.
change.relaxed: This only affects backups written from now on. Object Lock retention that is already written can never be shortened or removed, so everything already stored stays locked for its full original period.
change.disabled: Backups written from now on will NOT be locked and can be deleted or overwritten. Anything already written under a lock stays locked until that lock expires.

effect.warningsTitle: Conflicts with the jobs writing here
effect.existingProtected_one: {{count}} stored restore point is under the current configuration.
effect.existingProtected_other: {{count}} stored restore points are under the current configuration.
effect.existingUnprotected_one: {{count}} stored restore point is not covered by the current configuration.
effect.existingUnprotected_other: {{count}} stored restore points are not covered by the current configuration.

apply.title: Stored backups
apply.description_one: {{count}} restore point is already stored here. Changing the setting above never touches it; this puts it under the current lock, counted from now rather than from when it was written.
apply.description_other: {{count}} restore points are already stored here. Changing the setting above never touches them; this puts them under the current lock, counted from now rather than from when they were written.
apply.needsEnabled: Turn immutability on and save it before it can be applied to stored backups.
apply.needsSaved: Save the change above first — this applies the repository's saved setting, not the draft.
apply.confirm_one: Locks {{count}} stored restore point in {{mode}} mode for {{days}} days, counted from now. In compliance mode this cannot be undone by anyone, and the storage is paid for until it expires.
apply.confirm_other: Locks {{count}} stored restore points in {{mode}} mode for {{days}} days, counted from now. In compliance mode this cannot be undone by anyone, and the storage is paid for until it expires.

add.title: Add repository

deduplicated.hint: Chunked + compressed on the share — saves space

direct.hint: Whole files, no dedup — less CPU, faster restores

add.storageModeNote: Turn dedup off when the share is on a dedup appliance/NAS, or when faster restores and lower CPU matter more than space.

s3.endpointHint: Only for S3-compatible storage — leave empty for AWS S3.
s3.endpointInvalid: Enter a full http:// or https:// URL.

immutability.label: Immutable backups (Object Lock)
immutability.hint: Every backup written here is locked in the bucket for the retention period and cannot be deleted or overwritten until it expires — not by this appliance, and not by anyone who takes over its credentials.
immutability.aria: Write backups under S3 Object Lock retention

modeHint.governance: An account holding the bypass permission can still lift a lock early. Protects against a compromised backup account while leaving a deliberate administrator a way out.
modeHint.compliance: Nobody can shorten or remove a lock before it expires — not the appliance, not the account root. Storage is paid for until the last lock lapses.

immutability.retentionInvalid: Enter a whole number of days between 1 and {{max}}.
immutability.existingNote: Applies to backups written from now on. Backups already in the bucket are not locked by this — put them under it from the repository's settings after it is created.

delete.title: Delete {{name}}?

delete.jobsBlock_other: <1>{{count}}</1> jobs still target this repository — repoint or remove them first.

delete.jobsWarning_other: <1>{{count}}</1> jobs currently target this repository. They will fail on the next run until re-pointed at another target.

share.label: SMB share for Hyper-V hosts
share.hint: Hyper-V backups are written by abr-vhdx-tool on the Hyper-V host, which cannot see a folder of this appliance. Share this folder over SMB and enter the path every host reaches it by; leave it empty if no Hyper-V VM is backed up here.
share.uncInvalid: Enter a UNC path: \\server\share, optionally with a folder of the share after it.
share.accountHint: The share must write as the user the appliance runs as (Samba's force user). Without an account, the hosts open it with the Hyper-V inventory's own.
